title: Centre-out lace square shawl
subtitle: A fingering-weight square shawl growing outward from the centre with radiating lace panels.
excerpt: A square shawl in fingering-weight wool, worked centre-out from an 8-stitch cast-on with four radiating lace panels, one along each diagonal. A simple 6-row leaf lace repeat fills each quarter. Finished size approximately 120 × 120 cm when blocked. About 450 g of fingering yarn.
sourceNotes: The centre-out square shawl construction is documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 2nd series (1886), §Shawls. The radiating lace panels following the four corner diagonals are a standard Victorian device for square shawls; leaf lace motifs of this type appear in Mary Thomas's Book of Knitting Patterns (1943), §Lace Stitches.

knitting.gaugeText: 24 sts × 48 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stockinette on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A construction that begins at the centre of a square shawl with a small cast-on and grows outward to all four edges via increases at four corner markers.
A length of smooth waste yarn threaded through all stitches on the needle at a given row, allowing the knitting to be safely ripped back to that point.

content.text: A
centre-out square
in fingering wool with leaf lace panels along each corner diagonal. Finished size approximately 120 × 120 cm.

The shawl begins with an 8-stitch cast-on at the centre and grows by 8 stitches per RS row (two yarn-over increases at each of four corner markers). Each corner diagonal carries a 6-stitch leaf lace panel that radiates outward as the shawl grows. Thread a
lifeline
every 50 rows. Budget about 450 g (about 1,800 m / 1,970 yards) of fingering wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 450 g (1,800 m / 1,970 yards) of fingering-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, 120 cm or longer

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

24 stitches and 48 rows to 10 cm over stockinette on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. At gauge the square grows by 8 stitches per RS row; each RS row adds approximately 4.2 mm to the side length. A 120 × 120 cm square requires approximately 285 RS rows and about 570 total rows at gauge.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on
Cast on 8 stitches. Place markers after sts 2, 4, 6. Work 4 plain garter rows to establish the centre before the first increase RS row.
Increase row (RS)
RS row: *k to marker, yo, SM, yo; repeat from * 3 more times, k to end. (8 sts added per RS row)
WS row: k all sts.

Once each quarter section holds at least 12 stitches (after approximately 5 RS rows), begin the leaf lace diagonal. Place the 6-stitch leaf panel centred on each corner marker in the body stitches of that quarter.
Leaf lace diagonal (6 sts, each quarter, RS rows)

Row 1: k2, yo, k1, k2tog, k1. Row 2 (WS): k all. Row 3: k1, yo, k1, k2tog, k2. Row 4 (WS): k all. Row 5: yo, k1, k2tog, k3. Row 6 (WS): k all. Repeat rows 1 to 6 throughout. The 6 stitches of the leaf panel stay fixed within the quarter; the surrounding plain garter stitches grow.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off across all stitches. At 120 × 120 cm the stitch count at cast-off is approximately 8 + (8 × 285) = 2,288 stitches.
Stitch count check-ins
After 50 RS rows: 8 + 400 = 408 stitches. Each quarter holds approximately 100 stitches plus 4 corner anchor stitches. The leaf diagonal should be clearly visible.
After 150 RS rows: 1,208 stitches. Side length approximately 63 cm. Roughly halfway to the finished size.
Common faults

Leaf panel shifted out of alignment: the 6-stitch leaf group drifted within the quarter as surrounding stitches grew. Place additional stitch markers flanking the 6-stitch leaf group on each side to keep it centred on the diagonal.
Blocking
Soak in cool water 20 minutes, press out in towels. Pin all four corner points to form a 120 × 120 cm square. Pin along all four edges. The leaf lace diagonals will open visibly under pinning.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. A 120 cm square takes at least 24 hours to dry fully in the centre.
What to try next
Replace the garter field between the lace diagonals with an allover eyelet mesh (yo, k2tog on RS rows). This gives a uniformly open square with the leaf panels as denser structural lines.
